question: Find employees whose salary is above the average salary of their own department
db_schema: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, department TEXT, salary REAL);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT e.name, e.salary, e.department FROM employees e WHERE e.salary > (SELECT AVG(e2.salary) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.department = e.department)

question: List products whose price is higher than the average price of all products in the same category
db_schema: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, price REAL, category TEXT);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT p.name, p.price, p.category FROM products p WHERE p.price > (SELECT AVG(p2.price) FROM products p2 WHERE p2.category = p.category)

question: Find the second highest salary among all employees
db_schema: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, department TEXT, salary REAL);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees)

question: Rank employees by salary within each department and show those with rank 1
db_schema: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, department TEXT, salary REAL);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT name, department, salary FROM employees e1 WHERE salary = (SELECT MAX(e2.salary) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.department = e1.department)

question: Find all customers who placed orders in both January and February 2024
db_schema: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, total REAL, order_date TEXT);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND o.order_date < '2024-02-01' AND c.id IN (SELECT o2.customer_id FROM orders o2 WHERE o2.order_date >= '2024-02-01' AND o2.order_date < '2024-03-01')

question: Show the name and total spending of customers, but only for those whose total spending exceeds 200
db_schema: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, total REAL, order_date TEXT);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.total) AS total_spending FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.name HAVING SUM(o.total) > 200

question: Find products that have never been ordered
db_schema: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, price REAL); CREATE TABLE order_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, order_id INTEGER, product_id INTEGER, quantity INTEGER);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT name FROM products WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_items)

question: Find employees who earn more than every employee in the Sales department
db_schema: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, department TEXT, salary REAL);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees WHERE department = 'Sales')

question: List all departments and their employee counts, including departments with no employees
db_schema: CREATE TABLE departments (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, department_id INTEGER, salary REAL);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT d.name, COUNT(e.id) AS employee_count FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.name

question: Calculate the running total of order amounts ordered by date
db_schema: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, total REAL, order_date TEXT);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT o1.order_date, o1.total, (SELECT SUM(o2.total) FROM orders o2 WHERE o2.order_date <= o1.order_date) AS running_total FROM orders o1 ORDER BY o1.order_date

question: Find customers who have placed orders totaling more than 250
db_schema: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, total REAL, order_date TEXT);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.name HAVING SUM(o.total) > 250

question: Find the number of employees in each department and the average salary, showing only departments with more than 1 employee
db_schema: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, department TEXT, salary REAL);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS emp_count, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

question: For each product, show its name, price, and how much more expensive it is than the cheapest product in its category
db_schema: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, price REAL, category TEXT);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT p1.name, p1.price, p1.price - (SELECT MIN(p2.price) FROM products p2 WHERE p2.category = p1.category) AS price_diff FROM products p1

question: Find pairs of employees who work in the same department
db_schema: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, department TEXT, salary REAL);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT e1.name, e2.name, e1.department FROM employees e1 JOIN employees e2 ON e1.department = e2.department AND e1.id < e2.id

question: List all products and indicate whether each product's price is above or below the overall average price
db_schema: CREATE TABLE products (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, price REAL, category TEXT);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT name, price, CASE WHEN price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products) THEN 'above average' ELSE 'below or equal average' END AS price_status FROM products

question: Find the employee with the highest salary in each department using a subquery
db_schema: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, department TEXT, salary REAL);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT e.name, e.department, e.salary FROM employees e WHERE e.salary = (SELECT MAX(e2.salary) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.department = e.department) ORDER BY e.department

question: Show the total revenue and number of orders for each month in 2024
db_schema: CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, total REAL, order_date TEXT);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT SUBSTR(order_date, 1, 7) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(total) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND order_date < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY SUBSTR(order_date, 1, 7) ORDER BY month

question: Find the names of customers who ordered product 'Widget'
db_schema: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, total REAL); CREATE TABLE order_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, order_id INTEGER, product_name TEXT, quantity INTEGER);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id WHERE oi.product_name = 'Widget'

question: Find employees whose salary is exactly the median salary
db_schema: CREATE TABLE employees (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, department TEXT, salary REAL);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees e WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.salary < e.salary) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employees e3 WHERE e3.salary > e.salary) OR (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.salary < e.salary) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employees e3 WHERE e3.salary > e.salary) - 1

question: Find the percentage of total revenue contributed by each customer
db_schema: CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INTEGER, total REAL, order_date TEXT);
ground_truth_sql: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.total) AS customer_total, ROUND(SUM(o.total) * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(total) FROM orders), 2) AS percentage FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY percentage DESC
